openings.claim: Separate clearance-setting from retention without deleting either: the spacer leaves the strap tension path. Drill/cut only supplied strips into two removable padded rim-clamps; projecting edges locate the hatch. Sequentially set lateral stop clearances with a supplied 1 mm card, then remove it. Attach both fabric straps across the 180 mm direction to independent clamp attachments; tether removable parts with cord. Comparator uses identical clamps/straps but places the clearance card beneath one strap contact during closure, coupling spacing to pressure; never restore that coupling in the candidate.
openings.discriminator: Rival: clamp friction and strap tension alone explain stability; separation adds nothing. Candidate predicts less opposite-corner lift at comparable tension while satisfying position, pull, reopening and seal requirements. Equal lift or worse displacement defeats benefit; inconsistent hand tension makes interpretation uncertain.
openings.probe: First verify accessible rim undersides, grip, strap reach and stops outside the seal footprint without altering hatch/trough. If feasible, use two comparator closure/pull trials: centered and right-rim-card disturbed. Then ten candidate opening/closure/pull cycles, final closure disturbed. Disturbance is the supplied 1 mm card at the marked right contact; only seal-contact continuity is exempt. Record ruler displacement/corner lift, 20 N sideways-pull response, stopwatch reopening and visible seal tears. Candidate passes only after ten cycles: within 1 mm of its mark, withstands pull, one-technician reopening within 30 seconds, no new tears. Comparator lacks ten-cycle durability evidence.
openings.uncertainty: Rim cross-section, hatch thickness and attachment clearance are unknown; four strips, six bolts and four pads must support stable removable clamps/stops. Both 250 mm straps must reach secure attachments. Manual tension matching is uninstrumented; two comparator trials cannot establish reliable causality. Ninety-minute fabrication and twenty-minute observation limits apply.

lineage.reason: Relation, comparative defeat conditions, probe, caveats and declared uncertain fit preserved.

decision: Retain as an unproven bounded probe. Poor grip, unavailable geometry, obstructed full opening or seal damage defeats it. Preserve hatch/rim/seal; no drilling, cutting, gluing or permanent deformation of hatch/trough, powered mechanism or unrecoverable loose parts. Unknown resources never relax constraints.
